domain_label: Cinematography — The 9 Transition Camera Tricks as Frame-Pair Constraints (cine)
purpose: A method for planning stitched-reel seams: each of the nine transition camera tricks (match cut, match-on-action, whip-pan, masked wipe, invisible cut, flash/exposure cut, speed-ramp into cut, snap-zoom, jump cut) specified as a PAIR of frame constraints — what the END frame of clip N and the START frame of clip N+1 must contain — mapped onto start+end-frame conditioned video generation, with shooting requirements, failure modes, and a beat-energy rule for picking the trick per seam, sourced honestly against the grounding files' FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tags.
assumptions: no generated footage or engagement data is supplied; every score is a heuristic prior and every technique definition is quoted from the grounding research (cinematography_lighting_camera.md), whose web claims come from search-result excerpts of the cited URLs because theasc.com, studiobinder.com, en.wikipedia.org, help.runwayml.com and higgsfield.ai were 403-blocked this session — the FACT tag there means corroborated by >=2 cited sources via excerpt

Higgsfield model names, parameters, durations and media roles are quoted ONLY from higgsfield_surface.md, which read them off the live MCP surface on 2026-07-03; nothing about the platform is stated from memory

per-model prompt-phrase effectiveness (does 'fast whip pan right, motion blur' actually render a usable whip on a given model) is UNTESTED until the credit run — the technique-to-prompt mappings are carried as [ESTIMATE] until then

the flash/exposure cut and the deliberate jump cut are carried as [ESTIMATE — standard editorial convention, not in fetched excerpts]; their definitions are craft convention, not excerpt-verified fact
the reel format is 3-6 s micro-clips stitched into 9:16 verticals per the owner brief; seam planning assumes that duration band and aspect
exclusions: the lighting grammar and lens-language detail (three-point, motivated light, negative fill, anamorphic cues) beyond what a seam's continuity variables must hold constant — that is the sibling cine lighting KB

re-enumerating the full Higgsfield model catalog, credit costs, or character-consistency surfaces — this KB cross-references only the dual-keyframe support facts a seam plan needs, per higgsfield_surface.md
audio bridge EXECUTION (music, VO, mixing) — the J/L-cut is planned here at the shot level and handed to the sound specialist
post-production editing-software mechanics (timeline tools, NLE operations) beyond where the cut point must land
any guidance for evoking a specific real person while hiding the face — the likeness closed-lane stays closed

glossary.definition: A cut joined by matching shape, composition or color between two different subjects — e.g. round watch face center-frame cutting to the sun at the same position [FACT — StudioBinder match-cut/transition excerpts, cine research S32-S34]. The luxury-reel workhorse: watch to sun, pool to champagne glass.

An action begun in shot N completes in shot N+1 — a door opening, a jacket swung on — so the motion carries the viewer across the cut; the strongest continuity illusion, requiring a pose match at the cut point [FACT — StudioBinder transition excerpts, S32-S34].

Whip (very fast pan that motion-blurs the frame) out of shot N and whip into N+1, hiding the cut inside the blur; direction and speed must match across the seam [FACT — StudioBinder whip-pan + transition excerpts, S26, S33-S34].

A foreground object or body crosses and momentarily fills the lens (passing car, pillar, shoulder, handbag), wiping to the next scene; the wiping surface's tone and texture must match across the cut [FACT — invisible-cut sources, S33-S34].

A cut engineered to be imperceptible by joining on frames with near-zero unique detail — blur, blackness, flat texture, or identical frames; the umbrella category whose two easiest AI-safe implementations are the whip-pan and the masked wipe [FACT — S33-S34].

A cut hidden inside a blown-white flash or a dip to black: clip N brightens to near-white (camera flash, headlights, sun in lens) or falls to black, and N+1 opens from that same extreme and settles into the new scene [ESTIMATE — standard editorial device; not in fetched excerpts, carried at convention strength].

Progressive acceleration inside clip N so the cut lands on peak motion, with N+1 opening fast and decelerating; the energy across the cut masks the seam [FACT on ramping — beverlyboy zoom-ramping excerpt S27; the seam pairing is ESTIMATE — standard practice].

A rapid crash zoom onto a detail ends clip N tight on it; clip N+1 opens on an ECU of that same or graphically matched object in the new context — effectively a motion-assisted graphic match [FACT on snap zoom — S27; the seam construction follows the match-cut sources].

Same framing, time skipped: identical camera and composition across the cut while pose, outfit or location changes — the rhythmic outfit-change reel staple; reads as style only when framing is truly identical [ESTIMATE — ubiquitous social-video convention; definition corroborated by transition guides S33-S34].

Video generation constrained by BOTH a start image and an end image, with the model synthesizing the motion path between them — 'accept both start and end images as constraints, then synthesize the motion path' [FACT — fal.ai Kling description excerpt S35]; on the live Higgsfield surface this is the medias[].roles start_image + end_image pair [FACT — higgsfield_surface.md, live MCP 2026-07-03].

This KB's planning unit: one transition = two still-frame constraint sets, the END-of-clip-N spec and the START-of-clip-N+1 spec, written as two image prompts sharing lighting recipe, lens language and the trick's match variables before any video is generated [ESTIMATE — high confidence; direct consequence of the dual-keyframe workflow, S35].

nodes.definition: Establish the inversion the whole KB reasons in. The film-craft law is that match cuts and invisible cuts 'need to take advantage of what is already present in the shots — they drive how the shooting is done' [FACT — StudioBinder match-cuts/transitions excerpts, S32-S34]. For an AI stitched-reel pipeline this inverts cleanly: the transition is chosen FIRST, and it dictates the last-frame spec of clip N and the first-frame spec of clip N+1, because start+end-frame conditioning makes both frames directly promptable [ESTIMATE — high confidence; direct consequence of the dual-keyframe workflow, S35]. Consequently a stitched reel's shot list is really a transition list: seams are planned before clip interiors, and every downstream prompt inherits its constraints from the seam decision.

included: the shots-serve-the-cut law and its AI inversion
transition-first ordering of the planning work
excluded: the concrete per-trick frame constraints (the nine trick nodes)
which model executes the interpolation (model-map node)

pros.claim: Choosing the transition first makes every clip prompt derivable instead of retrofitted
pros.example: deciding seam 3 is a whip-pan before writing clip 3 or 4, so both prompts carry the pan direction from the start

cons.claim: Transition-first planning front-loads decisions and resists mid-edit improvisation
cons.example: discovering in the edit that a calm dissolve would serve beat 4 better, after both keyframes were generated for a whip

failure_modes: writing clip prompts first and hunting for a transition afterward, leaving ends that cannot join
treating the shot list and the transition list as separate documents that drift apart
acceptance_tests: the plan lists one chosen transition per seam BEFORE any clip prompt is written, and cites the shots-serve-the-cut law as the reason

nodes.definition: Fix the variables every seam must hold constant regardless of trick: matching texture, color, and brightness across the cut is what sells the illusion [FACT — StudioBinder match-cuts/transitions excerpts, S32-S34]. In the AI pipeline this extends to the full look recipe: both keyframes of a seam carry the same lighting recipe (e.g. golden-hour rim or low-key practicals from the sibling lighting KB) and the same lens language (focal-length feel, depth of field, anamorphic cues) [ESTIMATE — direct application of the match law to promptable variables; the recipe vocabulary itself is FACT-sourced in the cine research sections 1 and 5]. A seam whose two frames disagree in color temperature, grain, contrast or bokeh character reads as a splice even when the shapes match perfectly.

excluded: the lighting recipes themselves (sibling lighting KB)
the QC procedure that verifies the match (its own node)

pros.example: writing 'golden hour backlight, warm rim, long soft shadows' identically into the end-N and start-N+1 image prompts

cons.claim: Strict look-matching narrows creative contrast between scenes, which some beats want

nodes.definition: Constrain every clip interior to ONE main camera move, named in industry vocabulary with a speed modifier. Multi-move prompts degrade coherence in current video models [FACT-1src — Kling prompting guidance excerpt S31, corroborated by Runway structure advice S30]; Runway's official guidance structures prompts as [camera movement]: [establishing scene] with terms like 'slow dolly in', 'truck left', 'arc right' and ALWAYS a speed modifier (slow/medium/fast/rapid) [FACT — Runway help-center article located, excerpts via S30, S48]. For seams this bites twice: the clip's one move must BE the transition's motion when the trick demands it (whip, snap-zoom, ramp), so the seam move and the interior move are the same budget item, not additive.

nodes.definition: Specify the graphic match cut as a frame pair. Definition: a cut joined by matching shape, composition or color between two DIFFERENT subjects [FACT — StudioBinder match-cut excerpts, S32-S34]. END of clip N: subject A framed so its dominant shape sits at a locked position X (e.g. round watch face center-frame). START of clip N+1: subject B of the same shape, size and position (sun, wheel, coffee-cup rim). The framing coordinates must be locked in both image prompts — position, scale and orientation of the shared shape are the match variables. This is the luxury workhorse (watch to sun, pool to champagne glass) and the least forgiving trick: nothing hides a positional miss, so it depends entirely on keyframe control precision.

included: shape/size/position/color match between two different subjects
locked framing coordinates in both prompts
excluded: pose continuation across a cut (match-on-action node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured keyframe positional adherence per model would set this trick's real success rate

pros.claim: A landed graphic match is the most elegant seam in the vocabulary and reads as authored cinema
pros.example: the round watch face at center-frame cutting to the low sun at the identical position and diameter

cons.claim: Zero tolerance: any position, scale or brightness miss is fully visible because no blur or occlusion covers it
cons.example: a sun rendered 20% larger than the watch face making the cut stutter instead of flow

failure_modes: describing the two subjects without locking shared position and scale in both prompts
matching shape but not color/brightness so the cut flashes
attempting a graphic match before keyframe adherence is proven
acceptance_tests: the seam spec states the shared shape, its frame position and relative size for BOTH stills, plus the shared look recipe
revisit_triggers: QC shows repeated positional misses at graphic-match seams
a composition-control feature (position conditioning) appears on the surface

nodes.definition: Specify match-on-action as a frame pair. Definition: an action begun in shot N completes in shot N+1 [FACT — StudioBinder transition excerpts, S32-S34]. END of clip N: a body or object motion clearly mid-arc — door half-open, jacket half swung on, foot mid-step. START of clip N+1: the SAME motion continuing from the matching pose, legitimately in a new location (the location may change; the pose may not). It is the strongest continuity illusion in the vocabulary, and it requires a pose match at the cut point: the exact limb position, object angle and motion direction must be written into both frame specs, because the viewer's eye is ON the moving element when the cut lands.

included: mid-arc end frame and matching-pose start frame
exact limb/object position spec at the cut

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: pose-control tooling or measured pose adherence would change this trick's feasibility tier

pros.claim: Motion carries the eye across the cut, so a matched action can even relocate the subject unnoticed
pros.example: a jacket swung on in the villa completing the swing on the yacht deck, pose-matched at the shoulders

cons.claim: Pose matching is the most anatomically demanding spec — small limb-angle errors read as a body glitch
cons.example: the trailing arm 30 degrees off between the two stills making the subject appear to teleport

failure_modes: writing 'she puts on the jacket' without the exact mid-arc pose in both prompts
cutting on a settled pose instead of mid-motion, losing the carrying energy
letting wardrobe or hair state differ between the two poses
acceptance_tests: the seam spec names the action, its direction, and the exact body/object position at the cut identically in both still prompts
revisit_triggers: pose-conditioned generation (skeleton/pose control) appears on the surface

nodes.definition: Define the umbrella category the blur-family tricks implement. An invisible cut is engineered to be imperceptible by joining on frames with near-zero unique detail: blur, blackness, flat texture, or near-identical frames [FACT — StudioBinder transitions + film-transition sources, S33-S34]. Frame-pair form: END of clip N is a frame with almost no unique detail; START of clip N+1 is a near-identical low-detail frame. The two easiest AI-safe implementations are the whip-pan (blur) and the masked wipe (occlusion) — both manufacture the low-detail frame deliberately rather than hoping for it. The umbrella matters for planning because ANY seam can be downgraded to an invisible cut when its primary trick fails QC: blur and blackness are always generatable.

included: whip and wipe as its two easiest implementations
invisible cut as the universal fallback seam
excluded: the whip and wipe frame specs themselves (their own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new generatable low-detail mechanisms or overuse evidence would reshape the umbrella

pros.claim: Low-detail joins are the most robust seam class for AI because there is almost nothing to mismatch
pros.example: salvaging a failed graphic match by regenerating both keyframes as blurred frames and cutting inside the blur

cons.claim: Overuse reads as evasion — a reel of only blur joins never shows an authored match
cons.example: five whip seams in a six-clip reel making the edit feel like one long smear

failure_modes: treating 'invisible' as automatic rather than engineering the low-detail frames explicitly
joining two low-detail frames whose blur direction or darkness level differs visibly
acceptance_tests: the seam spec states WHICH low-detail mechanism fills both frames (blur, black, flat texture) and matches its character across the pair
revisit_triggers: a reel's seam mix over-relies on invisible cuts
a new low-detail mechanism (defocus, smoke) proves generatable and joins the family

nodes.definition: Specify the whip-pan seam. Definition: whip out of shot N and whip into N+1, the cut hidden inside motion blur [FACT — StudioBinder whip-pan + transition excerpts, S26, S33-S34]. END of clip N, last ~0.3 s: a fast pan in a NAMED direction (say left-to-right) ending in full motion blur. START of clip N+1, first ~0.3 s: a same-direction pan decelerating out of blur into the new scene. Direction and speed must match across the seam; prompt both ends explicitly — end-N 'fast whip pan right into motion blur', start-N+1 'camera decelerates out of a fast right whip pan' [FACT on the phrasing pattern — cine research prompt-mapping table, built from Runway/Kling vocabulary S30-S31]. It is the most forgiving trick for AI because the blur hides frame mismatch — which is why it anchors the low-risk end of seam sequencing.

included: the ~0.3 s blur windows on both sides
the whip as the clip's single move
excluded: where exactly to trim inside the blur (trim node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: credit-run evidence on blur rendering quality per model would re-rank the whip's forgiveness

pros.claim: Blur forgiveness makes the whip the highest-yield seam under imperfect keyframe control
pros.example: two clips whose scenes share only palette still joining cleanly because the cut sits inside matched right-going blur

cons.claim: In 9:16 a horizontal whip traverses little frame width, and the kinetic jolt suits only energetic beats
cons.example: a serene quiet-luxury window scene ruined by a violent whip into the next clip

failure_modes: mismatched whip directions between the two clips so the seam visibly reverses
a whip prompted without speed so one side blurs less than the other

nodes.definition: Specify the masked/object wipe. Definition: a foreground object or body crosses and fills the lens, wiping to the next scene [FACT — invisible-cut sources, S33-S34]. END of clip N: something dark and large sweeps across and momentarily FILLS the frame — a passing car, pillar, shoulder, handbag. START of clip N+1: the frame begins fully blocked by a similar surface, which clears to reveal scene B. The sell is matching the wiping surface's tone and texture across the cut — a charcoal car flank cannot hand off to a beige linen shoulder. Classic staging: walk-bys and car passes, both native to the luxury genre. The wipe is the occlusion twin of the whip: where the whip hides the cut in blur, the wipe hides it behind a full-frame surface.

nodes.definition: Specify the flash/exposure cut, carrying its honest sourcing: this is a standard editorial device NOT present in the fetched excerpts — [ESTIMATE — low sourcing, high convention, per the grounding file's own tag]. END of clip N: the frame brightens to near-white (paparazzi camera flash, headlights, sun hitting the lens) or falls to black. START of clip N+1: the frame starts near-white or near-black and settles into scene B. The exposure extreme is the low-detail frame, making this a sibling of the invisible cut. The paparazzi-flash version is perfectly on-genre: the live Higgsfield surface carries paparazzi-themed presets (2000'S PAPARAZZI, CANDID PAPARAZZI, RED CARPET — verbatim preset names) [FACT — presets_show output via higgsfield_surface.md], so flash grammar already exists in the platform's own vocabulary.

nodes.definition: Specify the speed-ramp seam. Ramping — progressive acceleration/deceleration of motion or zoom within one shot — is sourced fact [FACT — beverlyboy zoom-ramping excerpt, S27]; its use as a seam device is [ESTIMATE — standard editorial practice, per the grounding tag]. END of clip N: the final beats accelerate (motion or zoom ramping up) so the cut lands on peak motion. START of clip N+1: opening beats of fast motion that ease out into the scene's tempo. Energy across the cut masks the seam; it pairs naturally with a whip or an action match. On the live surface, cinematic_studio_video_v2 exposes a native speedramp parameter (auto/custom/linear/slowmo/speedup/impact) [FACT — higgsfield_surface.md, live schema], making it the designated ramp carrier — prefer the parameter over trying to prompt a ramp on models without one.

nodes.definition: Specify the snap-zoom cut. Snap/crash zoom — a very fast focal-length change producing a sudden attention spike — is sourced fact [FACT — filmlifestyle/beverlyboy excerpts, S27]. Seam form: END of clip N is a rapid zoom toward an object or face, ending TIGHT on it. START of clip N+1 is an ECU (extreme close-up — a detail only, per the shot-size ladder [FACT — S36-S37]) of that same object, or a graphically matched one, in the new context. It is effectively a motion-assisted graphic match: the zoom's speed covers small positional error that a static graphic match could not, while the matched detail carries the meaning. The zoom is the clip's single move and must carry a speed modifier ('rapid crash zoom onto the watch face').

nodes.definition: Specify the deliberate jump cut, carrying its tag: [ESTIMATE — ubiquitous social-video convention; definition corroborated by transition guides S33-S34, per the grounding file]. Definition: same framing, time skipped — rhythmic and energetic. END of clip N: locked framing of the subject. START of clip N+1: IDENTICAL framing — same camera position, focal feel, headroom, background — with the subject's pose, outfit or location changed. This is the outfit-change reel staple. The trick's entire risk is framing drift: AI generations do not naturally hold an identical camera across runs, so the identical camera and framing spec must be written verbatim into every keyframe of the chain (and ideally the same background), because at a jump cut any framing wobble reads as an error rather than a style choice.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evidence on framing-hold techniques (same start image, reference elements) would firm up the discipline

pros.example: five outfit changes on the same terrace mark, cut on the beat, all sharing one verbatim framing spec

cons.claim: It is the only trick whose failure mode is indistinguishable from sloppy editing — drifted framing reads as error, not style
cons.example: the horizon line shifting 5% between outfit cuts, making the montage look mis-stitched

revisit_triggers: a framing-lock mechanism (seed reuse, reference image) proves reliable and changes the spec discipline

nodes.definition: Constrain every seam frame to 9:16 vertical geometry. Platform UI forces safe zones: keep critical content out of roughly the bottom ~20% (like/comment/share stack), right ~10% (action rail) and top ~15% (branding), leaving a usable core of about 15-75% of screen height, centered; centered composition beats horizontal rule-of-thirds in vertical because UI flanks both sides [FACT — vertical-video framing/safe-zone guides, S39-S41]. Seam consequence: the matched shape of a graphic match, the pose of an action match, and the target detail of a snap zoom must all sit inside the centered usable core in BOTH frames, or the match happens under the UI where nobody sees it. Horizontal moves also show less than in 16:9 [ESTIMATE — high confidence, direct geometry, per the grounding tag], which shortens whip travel and favors push/pull, orbit and vertical reveals at seams.

excluded: general vertical framing craft beyond seams (sibling cine KB)

nodes.definition: Fix how camera-trick language physically reaches the generator. No standalone camera-move parameter (dolly/pan/orbit as an enum) exists on ANY of the 28 video model schemas on the live Higgsfield surface — camera language must be carried in the prompt text, via presets, via cinematic_studio genre/speedramp parameters, or via motion_control reference video [FACT — absence read across all 28 schemas, higgsfield_surface.md 2026-07-03]. motion_control (Kling 3.0 Motion Control) animates a character image with the motion AND camera movement of a reference video — the strongest camera-trick replication lever: record a reference whip or orbit once and reuse it [FACT — schema]. nodes.definition: Gate every seam on a stills QC pass before video generation. The planning recipe is: generate the two keyframe stills, then QC the match — position, brightness, color, blur direction — and only then run start/end-frame video generation per clip [ESTIMATE — synthesis recipe from the grounding file's section 6.4, untested until the credit run, per its own tag]. The QC checklist is trick-specific: graphic match checks shape position/scale, action match checks pose, whip checks blur direction and intensity, wipe checks fill completeness and surface tone, flash checks exposure level, jump cut checks framing identity. A failed still is regenerated for cents; a failed seam discovered in stitched video costs two clip generations plus the edit round-trip. QC of stills is therefore the single highest-leverage credit-saving gate in the seam pipeline.

included: the position/brightness/color/blur-direction checklist and its per-trick variants
excluded: automated visual-similarity scoring tooling (not on the surface)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: credit-run data on where failures actually concentrate (stills vs motion) would rebalance the gate

pros.example: spotting the sun rendered off-center in the start-N+1 still and re-rolling it before any video call

nodes.definition: Place the physical cut correctly per trick. Trim each clip so the cut lands MID-MOTION for whip and action seams — inside the blur window for a whip, mid-arc for a match-on-action — or ON the matched frame for a graphic match [ESTIMATE — the grounding file's planning recipe, section 6.4, standard editorial practice]. The generated clips deliver more footage than the seam needs; the trim decides which exact frame joins. For whip seams the join sits where both sides are at full blur; for action seams where the pose matches; for graphic matches on the two matched stills themselves (which the dual-keyframe generation placed at the clip ends); for ramps at peak motion; for flash cuts at the exposure extreme. A correct pair of keyframes can still yield a visible seam if the cut lands a few frames early, on settled or decelerating motion.

excluded: NLE mechanics and export settings (edit specialist)

nodes.definition: Plan the audio glue per seam even though execution belongs to the sound specialist. A sound bridge — audio from N+1 starting before the picture cut (J-cut) or N's audio continuing over N+1 (L-cut) — is free glue for ANY visual transition [FACT — the match-cut sources list audio match cuts, S32-S34]. Seam form: end-N carries a rising sound motif; start-N+1 reveals that sound as diegetic in scene B (the roar heard over the watch close-up becomes the car passing). The bridge must be planned AT THE SHOT LEVEL because it changes what the frames should contain — the diegetic source of the bridged sound must exist in scene B's frame spec. This node writes the bridge intent into the seam plan and hands execution to the sound specialist; it never specifies music or mixing itself.

excluded: music generation, VO and mixing (sound specialist; the surface's generate_audio is speech-only per higgsfield_surface.md)

nodes.definition: Pick the trick per beat energy — the craft-judgment layer, carried as [ESTIMATE — synthesis of the sourced definitions; the mapping is convention, not excerpt-verified]. Calm/composed beats (quiet luxury, window light) take the elegant precision seams: graphic match, invisible cut, or a soft masked wipe. Kinetic beats (car pass, party, race) take motion seams: whip-pan, speed-ramp into cut, snap-zoom. Rhythmic montage beats (outfit changes, day-in-life) take jump cuts on the pulse. Reveal beats (location unveil, arrival) take masked wipes and flash cuts, whose occlusion/exposure RESET the scene. The selection also reads the emotional grammar of the underlying move (whip = kinetic energy, snap zoom = attention spike, ramp = flourish emphasis [FACT — movement-grammar excerpts S26-S27]): the seam's motion is itself a beat of the film, not connective tissue.

included: seam motion as an emotional beat
the ESTIMATE tag on the mapping

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: engagement or review feedback on energy-matched vs mismatched seams would firm the mapping

pros.claim: Energy-matched seams make transitions feel authored by the story instead of imposed on it
pros.example: a race sequence whipping between clips while the closing quiet scene dissolves through a graphic match to the sunset

cons.claim: The mapping is craft convention, not measured — a beat can legitimately support several tricks
cons.example: an arrival beat serviceable by crane reveal, masked wipe, or flash cut, where the map alone cannot decide

revisit_triggers: audience/engagement feedback contradicts a mapping row

nodes.definition: Order seam attempts by execution risk. Prefer whip-pan and masked-wipe seams EARLY in production because blur and occlusion are most tolerant of AI frame mismatch; reserve exact graphic matches for hero seams once keyframe control is proven [ESTIMATE — confidence medium, based on blur/occlusion hiding mismatch per the transition sources, carried with the grounding file's own tag]. The risk ladder: whip and wipe (most forgiving) -> flash and ramp (exposure/energy cover) -> jump cut (framing-hold risk) -> match-on-action (pose risk) -> graphic match (zero cover, highest precision). Sequencing matters because early seams calibrate how tightly the chosen models honor keyframes; spending the first credits on a hero graphic match gambles the reel's hardest shot on an unmeasured capability.

cons.claim: Risk ordering can defer the reel's signature moment indefinitely if early results stay noisy
cons.example: a launch deadline arriving with only forgiving seams shipped and the hero match still unproven

nodes.definition: Compose the per-seam go/no-go that gates video generation. A complete seam plan contains: (1) the trick, justified by beat energy and by the risk ladder's current tier; (2) the frame-pair spec — end-N and start-N+1 constraints with the shared look recipe and 9:16 core placement; (3) a model from the both-frames list whose duration band fits the clip; (4) the motion carrier (prompt phrasing with its untested tag, speedramp, preset, or motion_control); (5) a stills QC verdict; (6) the trim target and the sound-bridge intent. A seam is GO only when all six are present and QC passed; any missing element is a named no-go reason, not a silent gap. This verdict is the KB's hand-off artifact to the director/production specialists: it makes every seam auditable before credits are spent and every failure attributable to a specific element afterward.

conflict_axes.name: precision_match_vs_blur_forgiveness
conflict_axes.description: The graphic match and action match demand exact positional/pose control with zero cover, while whip, wipe and flash seams hide mismatch in blur, occlusion or exposure — the two families trade elegance against robustness under imperfect keyframe control.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: sequence forgiving seams first as calibration; promote precision seams to hero slots only after QC proves keyframe adherence

conflict_axes.name: beat_energy_fit_vs_execution_risk
conflict_axes.description: The trick a beat's energy wants is not always the trick current keyframe control can deliver — the selection map and the risk ladder can disagree on the same seam.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: risk tier wins early (substitute the nearest forgiving trick); beat fit wins after a passed precision precedent

conflict_axes.name: continuity_law_vs_deliberate_break
conflict_axes.description: Matching texture/color/brightness sells most seams, but the jump cut deliberately breaks temporal continuity for rhythm — continuity is a law with one licensed exception.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the break must be declared per seam and executed with framing identity; undeclared discontinuity is a defect

conflict_axes.name: one_move_coherence_vs_seam_choreography

conflict_axes.resolution_hint: shorten horizontal travel, center match variables in the 15-75% core, prefer vertical variants (vertical whip, crane, push/pull) where the beat allows

conflict_axes.name: stills_qc_cost_vs_direct_video_gamble
conflict_axes.description: Generating and QC-ing two stills per seam costs time and credits up front, while prompting video directly gambles larger video credits on unverified matches.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the stills gate wins for every seam: a failed still costs one image regen, a failed seam costs two clips plus the edit round-trip

conflict_axes.name: native_param_vs_prompt_carried_motion
conflict_axes.description: Some seam motion has a native parameter (cinematic_studio_video_v2's speedramp) while the rest rides prompt text whose per-model effectiveness is untested — a reliability gap between the two carriers.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prefer the native carrier when one exists; tag prompt-carried motion as untested and probe it cheaply before hero seams

conflict_axes.name: visual_seam_vs_audio_glue_ownership
conflict_axes.description: The sound bridge smooths every visual seam but belongs to the audio specialist, while its diegetic source must appear in this KB's frame specs — split ownership over one seam.
poles: seam plan owns the bridge intent
audio specialist owns the bridge execution
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the seam plan states bridge type and diegetic source in the frame spec; execution, music and mixing are handed off and never specified here

edge_cases.description: Clip N whips right but clip N+1's opening pan decelerates from the left, so the seam visibly reverses direction inside the blur
edge_cases.trigger: the whip direction was described in only one of the two prompts, or paraphrased differently
edge_cases.mitigation: encode one named direction and speed verbatim in BOTH prompts and QC the blur direction on both stills before video

edge_cases.description: A seam's end-frame spec is sent to a start-only model (veo3_1, veo3, kling2_6, kling3_0_turbo, grok_video, grok_video_v15) and the end constraint silently vanishes
edge_cases.trigger: model chosen by look preference without checking the both-frames list
edge_cases.mitigation: the go/no-go checks the model against the both-frames list read off the live surface; start-only models serve only non-seam clips

edge_cases.description: minimax_hailuo is run at resolution 512, which the surface documents as incompatible with end_image, so the seam clip loses its end frame
edge_cases.trigger: resolution lowered for cost on a seam clip generated with minimax_hailuo
edge_cases.mitigation: flag the 512/end_image incompatibility in the model map and keep seam clips on that model at 768+ [FACT — higgsfield_surface.md]

edge_cases.description: A 3 s seam clip is requested from seedance1_5 (min 4 s) or minimax_hailuo (min 6 s) and the duration is clamped, shifting where the cut point lands
edge_cases.trigger: duration chosen from the reel plan without checking the model's band; unsupported durations clamp to nearest allowed
edge_cases.mitigation: check the duration band per model before commit; wan2_7 is the only model reaching 2-3 s natively — route ultra-short seam clips there

edge_cases.description: A masked wipe joins a charcoal car flank to a beige linen shoulder, and the tone jump inside the 'hidden' cut is plainly visible
edge_cases.trigger: the two wiping surfaces were chosen for staging convenience without matching tone/texture
edge_cases.mitigation: spec the wiping surface's tone and texture identically on both sides and QC the two fill frames side by side

edge_cases.description: A match-on-action seam says 'she puts on the jacket' without the exact mid-arc limb position, and the two generated poses disagree at the cut
edge_cases.trigger: the action was described as an event, not as a frozen pose at the cut instant
edge_cases.mitigation: write the limb/object position at the cut instant (arm height, object angle, motion direction) identically into both still prompts

edge_cases.description: An outfit-change jump-cut chain drifts framing across generations, and the montage reads as mis-stitched error instead of rhythm
edge_cases.trigger: the camera/framing block was paraphrased between generations instead of reused verbatim
edge_cases.mitigation: reuse one verbatim framing block for every frame in the chain and QC framing identity (horizon, headroom, background anchors) before cutting

edge_cases.description: The flash/exposure cut is cited as excerpt-verified fact when the grounding file tags it [ESTIMATE — standard editorial device; not in fetched excerpts]
edge_cases.trigger: downstream prose drops the sourcing tag while restating the technique
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the ESTIMATE tag wherever the flash cut is taught, and upgrade only if a fetchable source later documents it

edge_cases.description: A graphic match is specced with the shared shape at the bottom fifth of frame, where the like/comment/share stack covers it on-device
edge_cases.trigger: the match position was composed in a 16:9 mental frame without the 9:16 safe zones
edge_cases.mitigation: state every match variable's position as % of frame height inside the 15-75% centered core in both stills

edge_cases.description: A seam prompt stacks a slow push-in AND a whip in one clip, and the model produces incoherent motion that ruins both the interior and the seam
edge_cases.trigger: seam choreography added on top of an interior move instead of replacing it
edge_cases.mitigation: make the seam's motion the clip's single move with a speed modifier; split any second move into its own clip

edge_cases.description: The edit cuts a whip seam three frames early, on decelerating half-blurred motion, and the join shows despite perfect keyframes
edge_cases.trigger: the cut point was placed by clip boundary instead of by the trick's frame condition
edge_cases.mitigation: trim to the trick's target condition — full blur for whips, matched pose for action, the matched still for graphic matches, peak motion for ramps

edge_cases.description: A speed-ramp seam is prompted on a model with no speedramp parameter, and per-model phrasing effectiveness is unknown, so the tempo mismatch across the cut is discovered only after generation
edge_cases.trigger: prompt-carried ramp assumed to work because the phrase appears in the mapping table, whose effectiveness is untested until the credit run
edge_cases.mitigation: prefer cinematic_studio_video_v2's native speedramp for ramp seams; when prompting a ramp elsewhere, run a cheap probe clip first and keep the untested tag until evidence lands

workflow.action: Write the reel's shot list as a transition list
workflow.description: Enumerate every seam (N/N+1 pair) before any clip content, citing the shots-serve-the-cut law
workflow.gate: every adjacent clip pair has exactly one named seam slot and no clip prompt exists yet

workflow.action: Choose the trick per seam from beat energy within the current risk tier
workflow.description: Map each beat's energy (calm/kinetic/rhythmic/reveal) to a trick family, then check the risk ladder allows it
workflow.artifact: per-seam trick assignment with beat + tier justification
workflow.gate: each seam names its beat energy, its trick, and the tier that permits it

workflow.action: Fix the continuity variables each seam holds constant
workflow.description: Assign one lighting recipe and one lens language to both sides of every seam, plus texture/color/brightness targets
workflow.gate: both keyframes of every seam reference the same recipe strings

workflow.action: Write the frame-pair spec for every seam
workflow.description: Author the end-of-N and start-of-N+1 still prompts embedding the trick's match variables and the shared look
workflow.gate: each pair carries the trick's constraints from its node definition, not a paraphrase

workflow.action: Place all match variables inside the 9:16 usable core
workflow.description: Position shapes, poses and details at stated %-of-height coordinates within the 15-75% centered core, clear of UI zones
workflow.gate: no match variable sits in the bottom ~20%, right ~10% or top ~15% of frame

workflow.action: Route each seam clip to a dual-keyframe model
workflow.description: Pick from the both-frames list with the clip's duration inside the model's band; flag minimax 512 and min-duration exceptions
workflow.gate: no seam clip is assigned a start-only model and no duration will clamp

workflow.action: Name the motion carrier per seam clip
workflow.description: Choose prompt text, preset, genre/speedramp parameter, or motion_control per clip; tag prompt-carried motion as untested
workflow.artifact: motion-carrier column on the seam plan
workflow.gate: every clip names one carrier and untested prompt phrasing is tagged

workflow.action: Write one-move video prompts with speed modifiers
workflow.description: Give each clip exactly one industry-vocabulary camera move with slow/medium/fast/rapid, the seam motion consuming that budget
workflow.gate: no prompt contains a second spatial move

workflow.action: Generate the keyframe stills and QC the match
workflow.description: Generate both stills per seam and check position, brightness, color, blur direction plus the trick-specific variable
workflow.artifact: QC verdict per seam with the still pair
workflow.gate: a failed variable regenerates the weaker still; no video runs on a failed pair

workflow.action: Run start/end-frame video generation per clip
workflow.description: Submit each clip with its QC-passed start and end stills to its assigned model, chaining job_ids where clip N's end feeds N+1's start
workflow.gate: every submission carries both frames in the correct roles

workflow.action: Trim each cut to its trick's target frame condition and attach the sound-bridge intent
workflow.description: Land whip/action cuts mid-motion, graphic matches on the matched still, ramps at peak, flashes at the exposure extreme; record J/L bridge and diegetic source per seam
workflow.artifact: edit notes + bridge intents per seam
workflow.gate: every seam states its cut condition and bridge type (J, L, or none)

workflow.action: Issue the per-seam go/no-go before final assembly
workflow.description: Verify all six elements (trick+beat, frame pair, model, carrier, QC, trim+bridge) per seam and record the verdict
workflow.artifact: seam verdict sheet handed to director/production
workflow.gate: every GO has all six elements evidenced; every no-go names its missing element

priority_rationale: The foundations come first because every trick is expressed through them: the transition-first inversion defines what a seam even is, the continuity variables and the frame-pair discipline define how a seam is written, and the dual-keyframe model map plus the one-move rule define what the live surface can execute; the nine trick nodes then each bind one transition to its END-of-N / START-of-N+1 constraint pair; the craft layer (vertical framing, surface limits, stills QC, trim, sound bridge, beat-energy selection, risk sequencing) turns specified seams into shippable ones; and the go/no-go verdict comes last because it composes every upstream element into the single auditable decision that gates spending video credits.

dominance_rules.rule: Higgsfield surface facts dominate memory and marketing claims
dominance_rules.rationale: model names, roles, durations and parameters were read off the live MCP surface; web-marketed features (50+ Camera Controls) are not parameters
dominance_rules.trigger: a seam plan names a model capability, duration or parameter
dominance_rules.action: quote only higgsfield_surface.md's surface-read facts and refuse capabilities not on the schemas

dominance_rules.rule: The both-frames model list dominates model preference for seam clips
dominance_rules.rationale: an end-frame spec sent to a start-only model silently loses the seam constraint
dominance_rules.trigger: a seam clip is about to be routed to a model
dominance_rules.action: require membership in the both-frames list; start-only models serve interior clips only

dominance_rules.rule: Blur/occlusion-forgiving seams dominate precision matches until keyframe control is proven
dominance_rules.rationale: whip and wipe hide AI frame mismatch while a graphic match exposes every miss
dominance_rules.trigger: a precision seam is proposed before any passed precision QC precedent exists
dominance_rules.action: substitute the nearest forgiving trick and defer the precision seam to a hero slot after calibration

dominance_rules.rule: The stills QC gate dominates direct-to-video generation for every seam
dominance_rules.rationale: a failed still costs one image regeneration; a failed seam costs two clips plus an edit round-trip
dominance_rules.trigger: video generation is requested for a seam without a QC-passed still pair
dominance_rules.action: hold the generation until both stills pass position/brightness/color/blur-direction QC

dominance_rules.rule: The one-move rule dominates choreography ambition in every clip prompt
dominance_rules.rationale: multi-move prompts degrade coherence in current video models
dominance_rules.trigger: a prompt accumulates a second camera move
dominance_rules.action: make the seam's motion the single move and split any other move into its own clip

dominance_rules.rule: Continuity match variables dominate stylistic variation across a seam, except at a declared jump cut
dominance_rules.rationale: texture/color/brightness matching is what sells the illusion; the jump cut is the one licensed break and it keeps framing identity
dominance_rules.trigger: the two sides of a seam diverge in look, or a discontinuity is proposed
dominance_rules.action: enforce one look recipe across the pair; allow discontinuity only as a declared jump cut with verbatim framing

dominance_rules.rule: The 9:16 centered core dominates compositional preference for match variables
dominance_rules.rationale: content in the UI safe zones is covered on-device, so a match placed there never lands
dominance_rules.trigger: a match variable is positioned near a frame edge
dominance_rules.action: move it inside the 15-75% centered core and restate its position in both stills

dominance_rules.rule: Native motion parameters dominate prompt-carried motion where both exist
dominance_rules.rationale: speedramp is a schema-enforced control while prompt phrasing effectiveness is untested until the credit run
dominance_rules.trigger: a ramp (or other natively supported motion) is planned via prompt text on a model that has the parameter
dominance_rules.action: use the parameter and reserve prompt phrasing for models without one, tagged untested

dominance_rules.rule: The grounding files' honesty tags dominate fluency in every definition
dominance_rules.rationale: flash cut and jump cut are ESTIMATE-tagged conventions and prompt-mapping effectiveness is UNKNOWN until tested; restating them as verified fact fabricates sourcing
dominance_rules.trigger: a technique or phrasing claim is written without its tag
dominance_rules.action: carry the FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tag from the research file and never upgrade a tag without a new fetched source

anti_rework_rules.rule: Choose every seam's transition before writing any clip prompt
anti_rework_rules.prevents: regenerating clips whose ends cannot join because the transition was retrofitted after the interiors were fixed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check the both-frames list and the duration band before writing an end-frame spec for a model
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering after generation that the end constraint was silently dropped (start-only model) or the duration clamped and the cut point shifted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Generate and QC the two keyframe stills before any seam video call
anti_rework_rules.prevents: burning two video generations on a pair whose position, brightness, color or blur direction never matched

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the whip's direction and speed verbatim into both prompts at spec time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a direction-reversed or speed-mismatched blur seam that forces both clips to regenerate

anti_rework_rules.rule: Spec the exact mid-arc limb/object position in both frames of every action match
anti_rework_rules.prevents: pose mismatch at the cut that no trim can fix, requiring both stills and both clips again

anti_rework_rules.rule: State every match variable's 9:16 core position before generating stills
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-composing and regenerating frames whose match sits under platform UI

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reuse one verbatim framing block across an entire jump-cut chain
anti_rework_rules.prevents: framing drift that turns the montage into an error and forces the whole chain to be regenerated against a new anchor

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record the sound-bridge intent and its diegetic source while the frame specs are still editable
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-opening locked frame specs later because the bridged sound's source was never placed in scene B

iteration_protocol.trigger: a seam fails stills QC on any match variable
iteration_protocol.action: regenerate only the weaker still against the same spec; escalate to a spec rewrite after two failed regens; never proceed to video on a failed pair

iteration_protocol.trigger: the credit run produces per-model evidence on prompt-phrase effectiveness (whip blur, ramps, snap zooms)
iteration_protocol.action: replace the untested tags with measured verdicts, update the motion-carrier choices, and re-rank the trick risk ladder

iteration_protocol.trigger: a re-read of the live Higgsfield surface changes end_image support, durations, clamping or the speedramp parameter
iteration_protocol.action: rebuild the dual-keyframe model map from the new surface read and re-route any pending seam clips

iteration_protocol.trigger: a precision seam (graphic match or action match) passes QC and ships cleanly
iteration_protocol.action: record the precedent, unlock the next risk tier, and let beat-energy fit override the ladder for matching seams

iteration_protocol.trigger: a trick repeatedly fails at the video stage despite passed stills (e.g. blur never renders)
iteration_protocol.action: demote the trick in the selection map for that model, swap affected seams to the nearest forgiving trick, and note the motion-domain gap stills QC cannot see

iteration_protocol.trigger: platform safe-zone geometry or the target aspect ratio changes
iteration_protocol.action: redraw the usable core, re-check every pending seam's match-variable positions, and update the vertical framing constraints

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fetchable source later documents an ESTIMATE-tagged technique (flash cut, jump cut, ramp pairing)
iteration_protocol.action: upgrade the tag, cite the fetched source, and revisit any hedged guidance the weak tag had softened
